description: Indian-first personalized nutrition app with budget-aware meal planning. Flutter mobile + Django REST backend + Firebase Auth + GPT-4o + USDA FoodData Central. Target market: Indian users who eat Indian home-cooked food and want realistic, affordable, culturally-appropriate meal plans.
intended_use: Feed this entire JSON document to an AI coding agent (Antigravity, Cursor, Claude Code, etc.) as the single source of truth for building the project. The agent should reference this document for every implementation decision.

primary_developer_constraints.experience: Developer is comfortable with Flutter but new to Django.
preferences_stated: Wants Django specifically for ORM ergonomics
Wants production-grade Flutter (Riverpod, MVVM, reusable widgets, single ApiClient, exception handlers, deep linking)
Wants rule-based recommendation engine first, AI layered on top
Wants module-by-module build with clean, precise prompts to coding agent

project_agenda.summary: NutriPlan personalizes daily meal plans (breakfast/lunch/dinner) based on a user's biometrics, dietary pattern, allergies, and cuisine preferences. It tracks adherence, auto-aggregates calorie and micronutrient intake, and provides an AI chatbot that turns 'what's in my fridge' into actual recipes with validated macros.
project_agenda.core_thesis: Western calorie counters fail Indian users (wrong food database, wrong portions, no budget awareness, no cuisine fit). NutriPlan is Indian-first by design: ingredient database includes Indian foods with household unit conversions (1 katori, 2 rotis), recipes are Indian home-cooking, meal plans respect daily/weekly food budget in INR. Rule-based engine first, AI for personalization and substitutions.
primary_user_goals: Tell the app about me once → get a meal plan tailored to my body, goals, and food preferences.
See today's meals with full recipes, then check off what I actually ate.
Track calories and macros automatically as I check things off.
When I have random ingredients in my kitchen, ask the AI what to cook.
v1_locked_features: Meal tracker with status: planned / ate_planned / ate_substituted / ate_custom / skipped
Auto nutrition logging and daily/weekly aggregation
AI chatbot: free chat mode + ingredient-to-recipe mode
Indian-first ingredient database with IFCT 2017 nutrition (USDA fallback) + household unit conversions (1 katori = Xg, 1 roti = Yg)
Ingredient-level nutrition (recipes have ingredient lists; macros computed, not stored)
Real-time meal substitution (swap one meal, same macros, same budget)
Custom meal logging (free-text description + mandatory calories + optional macros)
v1_explicit_non_goals: Hyper-protein-per-rupee optimization as a primary mode (post-v1; falls out naturally if data is structured right)

backend.ai: openai Python SDK v1.x (GPT-4o via Chat Completions with structured outputs)
backend.nutrition_reference: USDA FoodData Central API (free, requires api key)
backend.wsgi_asgi: gunicorn + uvicorn workers (ASGI required for streaming chat)

external_services.firebase_auth: Identity provider; issues ID tokens to Flutter; backend verifies via firebase-admin
external_services.ifct_2017: Indian Food Composition Tables 2017, published by National Institute of Nutrition (NIN/ICMR). Distributed via npm package @ifct2017/compositions v2.0.9 (MIT-licensed wrapper) and Zenodo (CC-BY 4.0). CSV vendored into apps/recipes/seed_data/sources/ifct2017/ for deterministic seeds. 528 measured foods covering Indian pulses, cereals, millets, vegetables, fruits, spices, eggs, fish, meat. Primary nutrition source for v1.
external_services.usda_fooddata_central: Fallback data source for ingredients not present in IFCT 2017 (Western imports, branded foods, refined sugars, dairy variants like curd/yoghurt/butter, B12 overlays). Used at seed time only, not in runtime hot path.

system_architecture.description: Flutter app → HTTPS with Firebase ID token → Django REST API → Postgres + Redis. Backend verifies Firebase token via firebase-admin SDK. Celery workers handle daily meal plan generation, nutrition aggregation, and OpenAI calls. OpenAI and USDA are called from backend, never from client.
data_flow: User signs in via Firebase Auth in Flutter → gets ID token.
Flutter ApiClient attaches Bearer token to every request.
Django FirebaseAuthentication class verifies token → loads/creates User.
Recommendation engine reads DietaryProfile + Recipe DB → produces MealPlan.
User logs meals → MealLog rows + DailyNutritionSummary updates.
Chat endpoint streams GPT-4o responses; macros validated against USDA before returning.

recommendation_engine.philosophy: Rules-as-policy, AI-as-creativity. Hard constraints (allergens, diet pattern, calorie window, prep time) enforced deterministically. Soft preferences (cuisine, variety, macro fit) scored numerically. GPT is a fallback for rare profile-constraint combos, never the primary engine.

steps: 1. HARD FILTER: meal_type matches, is_active=True, prep_time <= profile.max_prep_time_min.
2. DIET PATTERN HIERARCHY: vegan ⊂ vegetarian ⊂ pescatarian; omnivore = no restriction; keto and mediterranean strict.
3. ALLERGEN EXCLUSION: exclude recipes whose allergen_tags overlap profile.allergies (hard).
4. DISLIKES: exclude recipes whose ingredients match dislike text (case-insensitive regex).
5. CALORIE WINDOW: keep recipes within 75%-125% of slot_target (slot ratios: breakfast 0.25, lunch 0.40, dinner 0.35 of target_calories).
6. EXCLUSION: drop excluded recipe ids (used in regenerate).
7. VARIETY LOOKUP: find recipe ids used in this slot in last 7 days for this user.
8. SCORE each candidate: +30 cuisine match, +20*macro_match_score, -50 if in last_7_days, +seasonal_bonus (stub 0 in v1), + random tiebreaker 0..5.
9. Pick max-score candidate. Cap pool to 200 candidates for performance.
10. If pool empty after hard filters → raise NoSuitableRecipeError (M7 fallback hooks here).

when_used: Reasoning fallback: rule pool returns < 3 candidates → GPT generates custom recipe respecting constraints, persists as Recipe(source='gpt').
Substitution chatbot: 'swap chicken with paneer in today's lunch' → GPT rewrites, USDA validates macros.
Ingredient → recipe: structured-output JSON schema, USDA validation before return.
ai_layer.critical_rule: Never trust GPT macros. Always re-derive from ingredients × USDA before storing or showing.

properties.name: string
properties.ingredients: array of {ingredient_name (must match Ingredient.name in DB), quantity_grams (float), display_quantity (float, optional), display_unit_name (string, optional)}
properties.instructions: array of string (one step per item)

nutrition_math.bmr_formula: Mifflin-St Jeor: 10*weight_kg + 6.25*height_cm - 5*age; +5 if male, -161 if female, -78 if other.

backend_build_specification.intended_executor: AI coding agent (Antigravity / Cursor / Claude Code)
backend_build_specification.build_mode: Module-by-module, sequential. Do not skip ahead. Each module must pass acceptance before next starts.
operating_rules: One module at a time. Complete fully (code + tests + migrations + acceptance) before next.
No speculative features. Only build what spec says.
Ask before deviating. Surface ambiguity; do not silently substitute.
Pin every dependency to an exact version in requirements/base.txt.
Tests not optional. ≥80% coverage on services. Every endpoint has at least one test.
Service layer enforced. Views thin (parse → service → serialize). Business logic in apps/<app>/services/.
Never trust client-supplied user identity. request.user is sole truth.
Idempotency: POST /tracker/log, /profiles/onboarding, /auth/register upsert on natural keys.
Structured JSON logs in prod. Service functions log entry/exit at DEBUG (no PII), errors at ERROR with stacktrace.
Every model change ships with migration in same commit.
Code style: black (line 100), ruff (E,F,I,B,UP,N), mypy --strict on apps/ and core/.
Commits: one per module. Format: feat(<module>): <summary> or test(<module>): ...
Do not use SQLite, even in tests. Tests run against Postgres.
Do not use Django default User. Use custom one from M1.
Do not write business logic in serializers or views.
Do not call OpenAI or USDA from model save() or signals. Always explicit service call.
Do not hand-roll JWT verification. Always firebase-admin.
Do not store API keys in models or settings literals.

M1_accounts.goal: Custom User keyed by firebase_uid. DRF auth class verifies Firebase ID tokens. /auth/register and /auth/me.
M1_accounts.authentication_class: apps/accounts/authentication.py::FirebaseAuthentication — verifies Bearer token via firebase-admin, creates User on first auth, returns (User, decoded_token). Handles: no header → None; malformed → invalid_auth_header; verification fail → invalid_token; expired → token_expired.
M1_accounts.fixtures: firebase_token fixture in conftest.py monkeypatches verify_id_token to return fake decoded payload.

M2_profiles.goal: DietaryProfile (one per user). Onboarding endpoint. Backend computes target macros. Captures budget constraints and cooking habits for budget-aware meal planning.
M2_profiles.model: DietaryProfile with: age (13-100), sex (M/F/O), height_cm (100-250), weight_kg (30-300), activity_level enum, goal enum, diet_pattern enum, allergies ArrayField, dislikes ArrayField, cuisine_preferences ArrayField (each list max 50, items max 64 chars), max_prep_time_min (default 45), skill_level (beginner/intermediate/advanced). Computed: target_calories, target_protein_g, target_carbs_g, target_fat_g, target_fiber_g. save() always recomputes via core.utils.nutrition_math.compute_targets — never accepts client-supplied targets.

endpoints.POST /api/v1/profiles/onboarding: upsert, returns full profile with computed targets
endpoints.PATCH /api/v1/profiles/me: partial update, recomputes targets, invalidates today's MealPlan cache (TODO comment in M2)

additional_fields.household_size: PositiveSmallIntegerField(1-12, default=1) — informational v1; family-sync in v2
additional_fields.cooking_frequency: CharField enum: daily | weekends_only | rarely — affects meal plan structure (rarely → batch-cookable recipes preferred)
additional_fields.cuisine_preferences: Split into primary_cuisine_region (CharField, single required: north_indian/south_indian/east_indian/west_indian) + secondary_cuisine_preferences (ArrayField, multi optional: punjabi/gujarati/maharashtrian/bengali/tamil/kerala/andhra/rajasthani/goan/sindhi/continental/chinese_indo/pan_asian). Union of both fields forms the full cuisine controlled vocab used by M3 recipe.cuisine and M4 engine scoring.
additional_fields.budget_derivation_rule: At least ONE of weekly_food_budget_inr / daily_food_budget_inr is required. Validated in service layer, not serializer. If only weekly given: daily = weekly/7. If only daily given: weekly = daily*7. If both given: weekly must equal daily*7 ±5%.

M2_profiles.onboarding_step_note: Step 5 (formerly step 6) now combines 'Budget and cooking constraints': budget fields + household_size + cooking_frequency + max_prep_time_min + skill_level.

M3_recipes.goal: Ingredient-level recipe database. ~150 ingredients (IFCT 2017 primary, USDA fallback) + ~80 household unit conversions + ~100 curated Indian recipes. Recipes store ingredient lists; nutrition computed from ingredients.

Ingredient.name: CharField unique (English, e.g. 'paneer', 'basmati rice', 'toor dal')
Ingredient.category: CharField enum: grain | pulse | vegetable | fruit | dairy | meat | fish | egg | oil_fat | spice | nut_seed | sweetener | beverage | processed
Ingredient.per_100g_nutrition: JSONField — required keys: calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g; optional micros: iron_mg, calcium_mg, vit_c_mg, vit_d_iu, potassium_mg, sodium_mg, magnesium_mg, zinc_mg, vit_b12_ug, folate_ug, vit_a_iu
Ingredient.approximate_price_inr_per_kg: DecimalField max_digits=7 decimal_places=2 null=True (some like salt/spices have no useful per-kg price)
Ingredient.allergen_tags: ArrayField of controlled vocab allergen choices
Ingredient.form: CharField enum: raw | cooked | as_eaten — declares what state the per_100g_nutrition reflects. Required. 'raw' for cookable items (rice, dal, atta, meats), 'as_eaten' for items eaten as-is (most fruits, raw vegetables, dairy). 'cooked' used only when nutrition data source measured the cooked form (rare in IFCT/USDA).
Ingredient.cooked_yield_ratio: DecimalField max_digits=4 decimal_places=2 default=1.00 — raw-to-cooked weight ratio. Rice ~3.0, dal ~3.0, atta ~1.5, meats ~0.75. Used by household-unit display layer when converting cooked-portion display to raw-weight stored. Set to 1.00 for as_eaten items.
Ingredient.source: CharField enum: ifct | usda | manual | composed — provenance of nutrition data
Ingredient.ifct_code: CharField max_length=10 blank=True (populated only when source='ifct')
Ingredient.ifct_name: CharField max_length=200 blank=True (the IFCT food name; populated only when source='ifct')
Ingredient.ifct_regn: PositiveSmallIntegerField null=True (regional sample count 1-6; populated only when source='ifct')
Ingredient.usda_fdc_id: IntegerField null=True (USDA Foundation Food ID if source='usda')
Ingredient.usda_description: CharField max_length=200 blank=True (populated only when source='usda')
Ingredient.extracted_at: DateField null=True (when the seed value was extracted from source)
Ingredient.confidence: CharField enum: exact | good | approximate | weak — how well the source entry matches this ingredient

HouseholdUnit.name: CharField (e.g. 'katori', 'roti', 'idli', 'dosa', 'cup', 'tbsp')
HouseholdUnit.ingredient: FK to Ingredient null=True — null = generic unit (cup, tbsp); set = ingredient-specific (1 katori dal ≠ 1 katori rice)
HouseholdUnit.grams: DecimalField max_digits=7 decimal_places=2 — weight in grams of 1 unit

Recipe.unchanged_fields: name, slug, meal_type, cuisine, diet_tags, allergen_tags, prep_time_min, cook_time_min, servings, instructions (JSONField list of steps), image_url, is_active
Recipe.REMOVED: calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g, micronutrients — these are now COMPUTED
Recipe.name_alt: CharField max_length=200 blank=True default='' — alternate/English name for regional recipe names (e.g. 'Mashed potato rice' for 'Aloo bhate bhat'). Included in search filter.
Recipe.estimated_difficulty: CharField enum: beginner | intermediate | advanced, default='intermediate' — filterable in list endpoint
Recipe.spice_level: CharField enum: mild | medium | hot | very_hot, default='medium' — filterable in list endpoint
Recipe.cached_nutrition: JSONField — populated by compute_nutrition service; schema: {calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, fiber_g, micronutrients: {...}, computed_at: iso8601}
Recipe.cached_calories_per_serving: PositiveIntegerField null=True — denormalized from cached_nutrition.calories for SQL filtering in M4 engine calorie window. B-tree indexed. Populated by compute_nutrition alongside cached_nutrition.
Recipe.cached_cost_inr: DecimalField max_digits=7 decimal_places=2 null=True — sum of ingredient prices × quantities
Recipe.cost_known: BooleanField default False — set by compute_nutrition; True when ≥80% of total RecipeIngredient.quantity_grams maps to Ingredients with non-NULL price

RecipeIngredient.ingredient: FK to Ingredient (NOT a name string — must reference real Ingredient row)
RecipeIngredient.quantity_grams: DecimalField max_digits=7 decimal_places=2 (canonical; stored in grams)
RecipeIngredient.display_quantity: DecimalField max_digits=6 decimal_places=2 (what to show, e.g. 1.5)
RecipeIngredient.display_unit: FK to HouseholdUnit null=True (e.g. 'katori'; null = grams)
RecipeIngredient.validation: quantity_grams is the canonical source of truth for nutrition computation. display_quantity and display_unit are for UI presentation only. Seed import and admin writes log a WARNING at INFO level if quantity_grams differs from display_quantity × display_unit.grams by more than 5%, but do NOT block the write. This allows HouseholdUnit.grams values to be updated over time without breaking previously-imported recipes.

services.compute_nutrition: apps/recipes/services/recipes.py::compute_nutrition(recipe) -> dict: sums ingredient nutrition × quantities; updates Recipe.cached_nutrition and Recipe.cached_cost_inr; writes computed_at timestamp. Also sets Recipe.cost_known=True if ≥80% of total ingredient weight_grams has a non-NULL approximate_price_inr_per_kg on its Ingredient, else cost_known=False.
services.recompute_nutrition_for_ingredient_chang: recompute_nutrition_for_ingredient_change(ingredient_id): finds all recipes using this ingredient, recomputes each. Called when Ingredient.per_100g_nutrition or price changes.

files: apps/recipes/seed_data/ingredients.json (~150 entries; columns: name, name_hi, category, source, usda_fdc_id, per_100g_nutrition (nested), approximate_price_inr_per_kg, price_as_of_month, allergen_tags)
apps/recipes/seed_data/household_units.json (~80 entries; columns: name, ingredient_name (or null), grams)
apps/recipes/seed_data/recipes.json (~100 entries; AI-generated candidates that user manually validates)
recipe_generation_workflow: User runs offline script (scripts/generate_seed_recipes.py — agent builds in M3) that prompts GPT-4o or Claude with recipe schema + batch of 10 dish names per request. Script returns JSON.
User manually reviews each recipe (ingredient quantities, cultural correctness, completeness). Reviewed recipes appended to recipes.json and committed to git.
M3 seed command (python manage.py seed_recipes) loads ingredients.json + household_units.json + recipes.json idempotently. LLM never writes to production DB directly.

Validation gate in seed_recipes: every Recipe's ingredients must reference an existing Ingredient row by name; fail loudly with missing ingredient name(s). Every quantity_grams must be positive. Every recipe must produce plausible kcal/serving (50 ≤ calories/serving ≤ 1200) — anything outside flags for manual review.
seed_strategy.command: python manage.py seed_recipes (idempotent, upserts by slug)

query_params: spice_level (exact match: mild | medium | hot | very_hot)
includes_ingredients (comma list of ingredient names; recipe must use all)
excludes_ingredients (comma list; recipe must use none)
GET /api/v1/recipes/.response: slim RecipeListSerializer (name, name_alt, slug, image, cached_nutrition summary, prep_time, estimated_difficulty, spice_level, tags, cached_cost_inr)

endpoints.GET /api/v1/recipes/<slug>/: full RecipeDetailSerializer including ingredient list (with HouseholdUnit display), instructions, cached_nutrition with micronutrients

M4_mealplans.goal: Rule-based engine picks one recipe per slot for a date. Persist as MealPlan.
M4_mealplans.model: MealPlan: user FK, plan_date (indexed), breakfast/lunch/dinner FKs to Recipe (nullable, SET_NULL), generated_by (rules/ai), generated_at, regeneration_count JSONField. unique_together (user, plan_date). Index (user, -plan_date).
M4_mealplans.engine_location: apps/mealplans/services/recommendation.py — select_recipe(profile, slot, plan_date, exclude_recipe_ids=None) pure-ish function.

score_weights.budget_fit: 25 (penalty applied if meal_cost > slot_budget; magnitude proportional to overshoot)

algorithm_constants.budget_step_note: Step 5.5 BUDGET WINDOW (inserted after calorie window, before exclusion): keep recipes where (cached_cost_inr / servings) ≤ slot_budget_inr × 1.15 (15% grace). slot_budget_inr = profile.daily_food_budget_inr × SLOT_BUDGET_RATIO[slot]. If pool empty after this filter, log 'budget_too_tight' at INFO and relax to 1.40× as fallback.

null_price_handling.policy: Recipes have cost_known=true only if ≥80% of total ingredient weight has a non-NULL approximate_price_inr_per_kg. Recipes with cost_known=false are EXCLUDED from budget-strict scoring (step 5.5) when the budget filter is at 1.15× ratio. They are INCLUDED when the budget filter relaxes to 1.40× (fallback) so the pool is never empty.
null_price_handling.field_addition_to_Recipe: cost_known: BooleanField default False (set by compute_nutrition service based on the 80% weight threshold)
null_price_handling.rationale: Spices, salt, water, and small-quantity ingredients commonly have NULL prices. Recipes whose cost is dominated by priced ingredients (rice, dal, paneer, vegetables) remain budget-comparable; recipes where most of the weight is unpriced (e.g. mostly spice-based) shouldn't be filtered by an unreliable cost estimate.

errors.NoSuitableRecipeError: raised when pool empty after hard filters. View returns 422 NO_SUITABLE_RECIPE. M7 hooks AI fallback here.

ifct_known_gaps_v1: No vitamin B12 measurements (anywhere in IFCT). Use USDA B12 overlay for animal products; treat plant items as 0 μg.
Vitamin D fields exist but most values are 0 — IFCT did not widely measure D. Do not surface D in MVP UI.
Dairy coverage limited to cow milk, buffalo milk, paneer, khoa. Use USDA for curd/dahi, butter, ghee variants, cheese, cream, condensed milk, toned milk, etc.
Sugars limited to jaggery and sugarcane juice. Use USDA for refined sugar, honey, brown sugar, palm jaggery.

Western vegetables (broccoli, zucchini, bell peppers, iceberg, asparagus, kale) absent. Use USDA fallback.
Cinnamon noted as absent from IFCT spice group during investigation. Use USDA fallback.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Service layer enforced; views stay thin
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Business logic testable without HTTP; easy to refactor; aligns with Django best practice for non-trivial apps.

design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: M7 streaming requires it; splitting now is premature optimization. Revisit if sync-endpoint latency becomes an issue.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Curated seed JSON instead of importing public dataset
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Faster v1 ship; quality control. Switch to public dataset import (RecipeNLG/Food.com) if scale demands.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Ingredient-level nutrition, not recipe-level (PERMANENT — v1 and forever)
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Recipes store ingredient lists with quantities. Nutrition is computed from Ingredient × quantity × per-100g macros, cached as a JSONB column on Recipe. This is the only architecture that supports substitution ('swap paneer for tofu' recomputes nutrition), portion scaling, budget-aware optimization (sum ingredient costs), and user-added custom recipes. Recipe-level storage (baked-in macros) makes all of these impossible and forces a painful migration later. Pay the M3 cost now.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: IFCT 2017 as primary nutrition source, USDA as fallback
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Indian Food Composition Tables 2017 (NIN/ICMR) provides measured per-100g-raw nutrition for 528 Indian foods — pulses, cereals, millets, vegetables, fruits, spices, eggs, fish, meat. IFCT measurements use Indian cultivars, Indian soil, Indian cooking ingredients. USDA Foundation Foods measures US cultivars, US fortification levels, US portion sizes. For an Indian-first app, IFCT data is more accurate for the core ingredient set. USDA fills known IFCT gaps: dairy beyond paneer/khoa, vitamin B12 (absent in IFCT entirely), refined sugar, Western vegetables (broccoli, zucchini, kale), and branded/processed foods. CSV vendored at apps/recipes/seed_data/sources/ifct2017/index.csv for deterministic seeds — no runtime npm dependency.

design_decisions_and_rationale.decision: Raw-weight storage, cooked-portion display (PERMANENT — v1 and forever)
design_decisions_and_rationale.rationale: Nutrition data sources (IFCT, USDA) measure raw ingredients per 100g. Recipe ingredients store quantity_grams in RAW weight (atta 50g, ghee 8g, etc.). Recipe nutrition is computed once at seed time by summing (quantity_grams × per-100g-raw nutrition) and dividing by servings; result cached on Recipe.cached_nutrition_per_serving. Users never see raw weights or per-100g values. Every user-facing nutrition number (meal cards, recipe detail, daily totals) is the cooked, plated, ready-to-eat portion. Display units use household quantities (1 katori, 2 rotis, 1 tbsp); grams visible only on expanded ingredient view. This separation lets us use measured raw-ingredient nutrition data (the only reliable kind) while presenting the cooked-portion mental model users expect.

things_to_explicitly_avoid: Do not use SQLite anywhere, including tests.
Do not use Django's default User model.
Do not put business logic in serializers or views.
Do not call external APIs from model save() or signals.
Do not silently substitute features the spec didn't ask for.
Do not add libraries beyond the stated tech_stack without asking.
Do not start a new module before previous module's acceptance criteria pass.

Do not store calories/protein/carbs/fat directly on Recipe as canonical fields. They live on Ingredient. Recipe has a cached_nutrition JSONB column populated by services/recipes/compute_nutrition.py, invalidated when ingredients change.

Do not store nutrition values per-100g-COOKED in the Ingredient model. All Ingredient.per_100g_nutrition is per-100g of the form declared in Ingredient.form (typically 'raw' for cookable items, 'as_eaten' for raw-eaten items like fruits). Recipe ingredient quantity_grams is raw weight matched to ingredient.form. The household-unit display layer converts cooked-portion display weights back to raw via Ingredient.cooked_yield_ratio.

When ambiguous, surface the question — never invent.
Stay within tech_stack. New library = ask first.

agent_usage_instructions.build_sequence_summary: Backend M0 → M1 → M2 → M3 (seed recipes) → M4 → M5 → M6 → M7 → M8. In parallel, Flutter Sprint 1 can start after backend M2. Sprint 2 Flutter is light; Sprint 3 Flutter ramps after backend M5; Sprint 4 Flutter after backend M7.

recipe_data_architecture.philosophy: Three layers. Layer 1 is the curated foundation (data, built once, expanded slowly). Layer 2 is the algorithmic engine (fast, deterministic, no AI). Layer 3 is AI personalization (used sparingly, expensive, with validation). AI is never the primary engine.

layer_1_curated_library.contents: ~150 ingredients (IFCT 2017 primary + USDA fallback nutrition + manual household unit conversions + approximate INR price per kg) + ~100 recipes (LLM-generated candidates, human-validated, ingredient list + portions + method)
layer_1_curated_library.source_of_truth_for: all nutrition data — recipes do NOT store macros; macros are computed from ingredients

layer_2_engine.contents: Pure-Python service: generate_week(profile) and substitute_meal(recipe, profile). No LLM calls. Optimizes for macros AND budget. Runs in milliseconds per user. Used by the weekly Celery cron in M6.
layer_2_engine.fallback_behavior: If no recipe in Layer 1 satisfies constraints, raise NoSuitableRecipeError; M7 may hook AI fallback here.

layer_3_ai.contents: GPT-4o for chat, custom recipe generation (with USDA validation), smart substitutions with reasoning. Outputs that pass validation may be promoted into Layer 1 (recipes with source='ai_generated').
layer_3_ai.critical_rule: Layer 3 is opt-in and per-request. The weekly meal plan cron (M6) NEVER calls Layer 3.

recipe_data_architecture.weekly_cron_flow: Every Sunday 8 PM IST (later configurable per user tz): Celery beat triggers generate_next_week_meal_plan for each active user. Task loads profile + last 2 weeks of plans, calls Layer 2 generate_week(profile, exclude_recent), stores MealPlan. NO LLM CALLS in this path. Pushable to thousands of users with one worker.
